//: The checks and the generators, typechecked.
Node has stripped TypeScript types on its own since 22.18, so
`node scripts/check-css.ts` runs with no build step and no
loader. That is what makes converting scripts/ cheap. It is
also the trap: stripping is not checking. A .ts file nothing
typechecks is a .js file wearing annotations, and it is worse
than the .js was, because a reader now believes the
annotations.
So this exists and `scripts/check-types.ts` runs it, which is
in check-all.ts beside every other check.
`noEmit` because nothing here is built: node reads the source.
`allowImportingTsExtensions` because that is how the imports
are written, `./schools-snapshot.ts` and `../shared/schools.ts`,
and they have to be: node resolves the real filename and has
no opinion about what TypeScript would have preferred.
`checkJs` stays off, and there is no JavaScript left in this
directory for it to check. It is off for what the imports
reach: `worker.js`, `aab/tools/stock.model.js`,
`aab/money/icons.js` and, through worker.js, most of
`functions/`. Turning it on reports 194 errors in the stock
model alone, in files this config is not the one converting.
What the rule actually wants is that scripts/ holds no
JavaScript, and `check-types.ts` says that directly. A .js
here again is a failing check rather than something somebody
notices a month later.
`allowJs` stays ON, which is what lets an imported .js be
INFERRED from. That inference is what a check here leans on,
and it is why COUNTS being all numbers is an annotation in
check-content.ts rather than a cast: it is checked against
the real object.
